meta.description: Canonical executable rules for the TrialGuard deterministic rule engine. Rules are grouped by category. Every rule carries a source_type that distinguishes SOURCE_DERIVED facts (confirmed in NCT01986881 / Wiviott NEJM 2019 / ICH E6(R2)) from SYNTHETIC_ASSUMPTION values (reasonable industry convention, not explicitly published for this trial). AI (watsonx.ai) NEVER makes the final deviation determination for any rule in this file. All evaluation is deterministic Python.

severity_definitions.major: Patient safety risk, eligibility violation, mandatory safety visit/data missed, blinding broken, or study drug substantially wrong. Must be reported and reviewed.
severity_definitions.minor: Non-safety visit window exceeded, required non-safety lab absent, dose compliance below threshold, secondary endpoint data missing.
severity_definitions.administrative: No patient safety or data integrity impact; process/documentation shortfall only.

comparator_semantics.present: actual IS NOT NULL (field exists and is non-null)
comparator_semantics.absent: actual IS NULL or value equals forbidden_value

rules.name: First Dose Dispensed at Randomisation
rules.description: The active-arm patient must receive dapagliflozin 10 mg at the randomisation visit (V-RAND). Absence of a dispensing record on randomisation day is a major deviation.
rules.condition: dosing_events.drug_code == 'DAPAGLI-10' AND dosing_events.visit_id == 'V-RAND' AND patients.arm == 'ARM-ACTIVE'

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Interventions: Dapagliflozin 10 mg oral QD starting at randomisation
protocol_reference.verbatim: Study drug will be dispensed to the patient at the randomisation visit. The first dose will be taken at the site.

rules.name: Drug Compliance ≥ 70 % at Annual Assessment
rules.description: Pill-count or e-diary compliance must be ≥ 70 % at each annual assessment visit (V-M12, V-EOS). Compliance < 70 % is a minor deviation; < 50 % for any rolling 90-day window escalates to major.
rules.condition: dosing_events.compliance_pct < 70 AND visits.visit_id IN ('V-M12', 'V-EOS')

severity_escalation.reason: Sustained non-compliance invalidates per-protocol population assignment.

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — standard Phase III drug accountability convention
protocol_reference.verbatim: Protocol compliance will be assessed by pill count at each annual visit. Compliance < 70 % should be documented as a protocol deviation.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: 70 % threshold is industry-standard for Phase III CVOT trials. The exact threshold is not published in the NCT01986881 registry or the Wiviott NEJM 2019 primary publication.

rules.name: Dapagliflozin Fixed Dose Integrity — 10 mg Only
rules.description: Dapagliflozin is a fixed-dose 10 mg tablet (ARM-ACTIVE). Any recorded dose other than 10 mg — whether a split, doubled, or transcription error — is a major deviation. There is zero tolerance: the tablet is not divisible.
rules.condition: dosing_events.drug_code == 'DAPAGLI-10' AND dosing_events.actual_dose != 10

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Drug: Dapagliflozin 10 mg; Wiviott NEJM 2019
protocol_reference.verbatim: The study drug dapagliflozin will be administered as a 10 mg tablet once daily. No dose modification is permitted.

rules.name: Oral Route Mandatory — No Route Substitution
rules.description: Dapagliflozin must be administered orally. Any recorded route other than 'oral' is a major deviation because route directly determines pharmacokinetics and the study is designed for oral SGLT2 inhibition.
rules.condition: dosing_events.drug_code == 'DAPAGLI-10' AND dosing_events.route != 'oral'

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Interventions: Drug: Dapagliflozin — Oral Tablet
protocol_reference.verbatim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg oral tablet administered once daily.

rules.name: Once-Daily Frequency — No Double-Dosing Within 24-Hour Window
rules.description: Each patient may receive at most one dapagliflozin dose per calendar day. Two dosing_events records for the same patient and drug_code on the same calendar day constitute a major deviation (pharmacodynamic overdose risk).
rules.condition: COUNT(dosing_events WHERE drug_code == 'DAPAGLI-10' AND DATE(administration_date) == target_date AND patient_id == p) > 1

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Interventions: QD (once daily) dosing
protocol_reference.verbatim: Dapagliflozin 10 mg administered once daily.

rules.name: Screening Visit Timing — Within 14 Days Pre-Randomisation
rules.description: The screening visit must occur within 14 calendar days before the randomisation date (Day -14 to Day -1). A screening visit more than 14 days before randomisation risks stale eligibility data (HbA1c, eGFR).
rules.condition: visits.visit_id == 'V-SCREEN' AND (randomisation_day - visits.actual_day) > 14

window_absolute.comment: Day 0 = randomisation. Earliest = Day -14 nominal minus 7-day grace = Day -21.

severity_escalation.reason: Eligibility lab results (HbA1c, eGFR) are more than 30 days old and may no longer reflect true eligibility status.

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — standard Phase III CVOT screening window convention
protocol_reference.verbatim: Screening procedures should be performed within 14 days prior to randomisation.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: 14-day screening window is industry-standard for Phase III cardiovascular outcomes trials. The exact window is not published in the NCT01986881 registry.

rules.name: Month 2 Visit Window — Day 53 to Day 67
rules.description: The Month 2 follow-up visit must occur within Day 53–67 post-randomisation (Day 60 ± 7 days). A visit outside this window risks confounding the early tolerability and safety assessment.
rules.condition: visits.visit_id == 'V-M2' AND (visits.actual_day < 53 OR visits.actual_day > 67)

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — standard Phase III CVOT Month 2 window convention
protocol_reference.verbatim: The Month 2 visit should be scheduled approximately 2 months (±1 week) after randomisation.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: Day 60 ± 7 is standard for Month 2 treatment visits in Phase III CV trials; exact window not published for NCT01986881.

rules.name: Month 6 Safety Visit Window — Day 168 to Day 196
rules.description: The Month 6 safety visit must occur within Day 168–196 (Day 182 ± 14 days). This visit is safety-critical for SGLT2-class renal monitoring (eGFR) and cardiovascular safety assessment. A missed or late visit is a major deviation.
rules.condition: visits.visit_id == 'V-M6' AND (visits.actual_day < 168 OR visits.actual_day > 196 OR visits.status == 'missed')

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC (window) — SOURCE_DERIVED (safety-critical classification based on SGLT2 class renal monitoring requirements and Wiviott NEJM 2019 renal composite endpoint)
protocol_reference.verbatim: The Month 6 safety assessment is mandatory. Sites should reschedule within the window if the visit is missed.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: ±14-day window for Month 6 is standard Phase III convention. Safety-critical flag is derived from SGLT2 class labelling (mandatory periodic renal function monitoring) confirmed in the dapagliflozin SmPC.

rules.name: Month 12 Annual Assessment Window — Day 351 to Day 379
rules.description: The Month 12 annual assessment must occur within Day 351–379 (Day 365 ± 14 days). Annual HbA1c and eGFR data feed pre-specified secondary and renal composite endpoints; missed data constitutes a minor deviation (or major if the patient is within 6 months of EOS).
rules.condition: visits.visit_id == 'V-M12' AND (visits.actual_day < 351 OR visits.actual_day > 379 OR visits.status == 'missed')

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC (day anchor and window) — SOURCE_DERIVED (annual assessments implied by 4-year trial duration in Wiviott NEJM 2019)
protocol_reference.verbatim: Annual safety assessments including HbA1c and renal function are required at 12-month intervals.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: Day 365 ± 14 is standard for annual visits in Phase III CVOT trials; exact window not published for NCT01986881.

rules.name: End-of-Study Visit — Must Occur Before or On Day 1461
rules.description: The End-of-Study visit must be completed by Day 1461 (approximately 4 years post-randomisation, matching the published ~4.2-year median follow-up). It may occur up to 30 days early. It is both a safety-critical visit and the primary endpoint data collection point; a missed EOS visit is a major deviation.
rules.condition: visits.visit_id == 'V-EOS' AND (visits.actual_day > 1461 OR visits.status == 'missed')

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC (Day 1461 anchor) — SOURCE_DERIVED (median follow-up ~4.2 years, Wiviott NEJM 2019 Table 1)
protocol_reference.verbatim: The end-of-study visit will be conducted at study closure. All primary endpoint data must be collected at this visit.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: Day 1461 (~4 years) derived from published median follow-up of 4.2 years. Exact EOS day is patient-specific in the real trial; this is a fixed anchor for the demo synthetic cohort.

rules.name: Prohibited Concomitant SGLT2 Inhibitors
rules.description: No other SGLT2 inhibitor (canagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, ipragliflozin, luseogliflozin) may be used concurrently for any duration. Any overlap — regardless of dose or duration — is a major deviation because it introduces pharmacodynamic redundancy and unmeasured safety interaction not evaluated in this trial.
rules.condition: medications.drug_class == 'SGLT2 inhibitor' AND medications.drug_name NOT IN ('dapagliflozin') AND medications.start_date <= patient.study_end_date AND (medications.end_date IS NULL OR medications.end_date >= patient.enrollment_date)

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Eligibility exclusion: patients on other SGLT2 inhibitors; Wiviott NEJM 2019 Methods
protocol_reference.verbatim: Concomitant use of other SGLT2 inhibitors is not permitted during the study.

rules.name: High-Dose Loop Diuretic — Requires Medical Monitor Notification
rules.description: Concurrent use of a loop diuretic at a dose equivalent to furosemide ≥ 80 mg/day (or equivalent torasemide ≥ 20 mg/day, bumetanide ≥ 2 mg/day) with dapagliflozin carries a risk of volume depletion and acute kidney injury. Initiation or dose escalation to these thresholds without documented Medical Monitor notification is a minor deviation.
rules.condition: medications.drug_class == 'loop_diuretic' AND medications.dose_mg_equivalent >= 80 AND medications.start_date >= patients.enrollment_date AND visit.monitoring_notification_recorded == false

severity_escalation.condition: Loop diuretic dose equivalent ≥ 160 mg furosemide/day AND no notification
severity_escalation.reason: High risk of acute kidney injury combined with SGLT2-mediated osmotic diuresis.

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — dapagliflozin EU SmPC Section 4.4 Special Warnings; standard SGLT2-class volume depletion guidance
protocol_reference.verbatim: Concomitant use of diuretics, particularly loop diuretics, may increase the risk of volume depletion. Medical Monitor notification is required if high-dose loop diuretics are initiated.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: Furosemide ≥ 80 mg/day threshold is derived from the dapagliflozin SmPC class warning. The specific notification requirement is not explicitly published in NCT01986881 registry entries.

rules.name: Warfarin Initiation — Requires Medical Monitor Notification and INR Monitoring
rules.description: Warfarin (or any vitamin K antagonist: acenocoumarol, phenprocoumon, fluindione) must not be initiated during the study without documented Medical Monitor notification. Once initiated, weekly INR monitoring is required. A new start without notification is a major deviation. This rule checks whether a warfarin record with start_date after enrollment exists without a linked monitoring_notification record.
rules.condition: medications.drug_class == 'vitamin_K_antagonist' AND medications.start_date >= patients.enrollment_date AND monitoring_notification.drug_code == 'warfarin' IS NULL

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — dapagliflozin FDA label (drug interaction: vitamin K antagonists); matches DEV-003/MED-007 scenario in root.md
protocol_reference.verbatim: Vitamin K antagonists should be used with caution. New initiation of warfarin requires Medical Monitor notification and weekly INR monitoring.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: Warfarin is not explicitly listed as prohibited in the published NCT01986881 registry. This rule is grounded in the dapagliflozin product labelling drug interaction guidance and is classified SYNTHETIC_ASSUMPTION for transparency.

rules.name: New Insulin Initiation — Requires Medical Monitor Approval
rules.description: Patients on background insulin at baseline may continue. However, new insulin initiation (no insulin at randomisation → insulin started ≥ Day 1) requires Medical Monitor approval. Unapproved new insulin initiation is a minor deviation because it confounds the glycaemic secondary endpoint (HbA1c change from baseline).
rules.condition: medications.drug_class == 'insulin' AND medications.start_date > patients.enrollment_date AND patients.baseline_insulin == false AND medical_monitor_approval.drug_class == 'insulin' IS NULL

severity_escalation.condition: New insulin started without approval AND patient had no baseline insulin AND HbA1c endpoint visit is within 90 days
severity_escalation.reason: Confounds primary glycaemic endpoint assessment in the per-protocol population.

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — standard Phase III T2D CVOT practice; new insulin initiation restriction common to SGLT2 inhibitor outcome trials
protocol_reference.verbatim: Background antidiabetic therapy should remain stable throughout the study period. New insulin initiation requires Medical Monitor approval.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: New insulin initiation restriction is a common Phase III T2D trial constraint to protect glycaemic endpoint integrity. Patients on insulin at baseline (30.7% per Wiviott NEJM 2019 Table 1) were explicitly enrolled; only NEW initiation is restricted.

rules.name: Screening HbA1c — Must Be Present and Within Eligibility Range 6.5–12.0 %
rules.description: HbA1c must be measured at the Screening visit (V-SCREEN). The result must fall within the eligibility range of 6.5–12.0 %. An absent result prevents eligibility confirmation (major). A result outside 6.5–12.0 % means the patient should not have been enrolled (major eligibility violation).
rules.condition: lab_results.test_code == 'HBA1C' AND lab_results.visit_id == 'V-SCREEN' AND (lab_results.result_value IS NULL OR lab_results.result_value < 6.5 OR lab_results.result_value > 12.0)

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Inclusion Criterion 2: HbA1c ≥ 6.5 % and ≤ 12.0 % at screening; Wiviott NEJM 2019 Methods
protocol_reference.verbatim: Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) value ≥ 6.5 % and ≤ 12.0 % at the time of screening.

rules.name: Screening eGFR — Must Be ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (CKD-EPI)
rules.description: eGFR calculated by the CKD-EPI formula from serum creatinine must be ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² at the Screening visit. This is an explicit inclusion criterion. An absent or below-threshold result means the patient should not have been enrolled. This is a major deviation in both cases.
rules.condition: lab_results.test_code == 'eGFR_CKD_EPI' AND lab_results.visit_id == 'V-SCREEN' AND (lab_results.result_value IS NULL OR lab_results.result_value < 60)

protocol_reference.citation: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01986881 — Inclusion Criterion 4: eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²; Wiviott NEJM 2019 Methods
protocol_reference.verbatim: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² at screening.

rules.name: eGFR Monitoring at Safety-Critical Visits — Must Be Present
rules.description: eGFR must be measured and recorded at all safety-critical visits: V-M6 (Month 6), V-M12 (Month 12 annual), and V-EOS (End of Study). These visits feed the renal composite endpoint (pre-specified secondary outcome: sustained ≥ 40 % decrease in eGFR). An absent eGFR result at any of these visits is a major deviation because it directly impairs endpoint adjudication.
rules.condition: lab_results.test_code == 'eGFR_CKD_EPI' AND visits.visit_id IN ('V-M6', 'V-M12', 'V-EOS') AND lab_results.result_value IS NULL

protocol_reference.citation: Wiviott NEJM 2019 — Pre-specified renal composite endpoint: sustained ≥ 40 % eGFR decrease, ESRD, or renal/CV death; eGFR monitoring confirmed in publication supplementary appendix
protocol_reference.protocol_section: Section 8.3 — Secondary and Renal Endpoint Assessments
protocol_reference.verbatim: Renal function (eGFR by CKD-EPI) will be assessed at all scheduled visits including Month 6, annual assessments, and end of study.

rules.name: Informed Consent Obtained Before Any Study Procedure
rules.description: A signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) record must exist for the patient before any screening procedure is recorded. The ICF date must be ≤ the earliest screening lab or procedure date. An absent ICF or an ICF signed after a study procedure is a major deviation under ICH E6(R2) GCP 4.8.1.
rules.condition: NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM consent_records WHERE patient_id = p.patient_id AND consent_date <= (SELECT MIN(actual_date) FROM visits WHERE patient_id = p.patient_id))

expected_value.timing: ICF date must be on or before the earliest study procedure date

protocol_reference.citation: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8.1 — Informed consent must be obtained before any study-specific procedures are performed
protocol_reference.verbatim: Freely given informed consent must be obtained from each subject before any study-specific procedure is performed.

rules.name: Protocol Amendment Re-Consent — Within 14 Days of Amendment Effective Date
rules.description: When a protocol amendment is issued, patients must re-sign the updated ICF within 14 calendar days of the amendment effective date. Re-consent > 14 days is an administrative deviation. Re-consent > 30 days, or any study procedure performed after the amendment without re-consent, is a major deviation.
rules.condition: amendment_reconsent.reconsent_days_after_amendment > 14 WHERE amendment_reconsent.patient_id = patient_id AND amendment_reconsent.amendment_id = amendment_id

expected_value.unit: calendar days after amendment effective date

severity_escalation.condition: Re-consent > 30 days after amendment effective date
severity_escalation.reason: Patient participated in study procedures under an unapproved consent version for > 30 days.

severity_escalation.condition: Study procedure performed after amendment effective date without re-consent
severity_escalation.reason: Patient performed protocol procedures without valid informed consent — GCP 4.8.2 violation.

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC (14-day window) — SOURCE_DERIVED: ICH E6(R2) GCP 4.8.2 re-consent requirement after protocol amendment; matches CONSENT-001/DEV-007 in root.md
protocol_reference.verbatim: In the event of a protocol amendment, patients must re-sign the updated informed consent form within 14 days of the amendment effective date.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: The 14-day re-consent window is standard industry practice. ICH E6(R2) mandates re-consent but does not specify an exact day limit; 14 days is the assumed threshold for this trial.

rules.name: eCRF Data Entry — Within 5 Business Days of Visit
rules.description: All eCRF data for a visit must be entered within 5 business days of the visit date (data_entry_date − actual_date ≤ 5 business days). Late entry > 5 business days is an administrative deviation. A site-level pattern of ≥ 3 consecutive visits with lag > 10 business days escalates to a minor site-level deviation and triggers a site risk score component increase.
rules.condition: BUSINESS_DAYS(visits.data_entry_date, visits.actual_date) > 5

severity_escalation.condition: ≥ 3 consecutive visits at the same site with lag > 10 business days
severity_escalation.reason: Systematic data entry lag indicates a site-level process failure; increases site risk score DataDelay component.

protocol_reference.citation: SYNTHETIC — standard Phase III eCRF data entry timeliness standard; matches DATA-002/DEV-010 in root.md
protocol_reference.verbatim: All data must be entered into the eCRF within 5 business days of the visit or procedure date.
protocol_reference.assumption_note: 5-business-day eCRF entry requirement is common in Phase III sponsor SOPs. The exact threshold is not published in the NCT01986881 registry.
